texts: mixed: the lighting event, both groups, the time terms and the tense all land, but two records are weak - "day 300 of Year 1" becomes a day-of-month term, the only day granularity the instruction set defines, and "the keepers of the Harbor Row" falls between a possessive genitive and an agent noun's of-object, so the link head is undetermined. For the second, a minimal edit makes it deterministic: "On day 300 of Year 1, the Harbor Row keepers together lit the lanterns of the Harbor Row at sundown." The day-of-year date has no licensed form at all, and "together" leaves no positive atom - the collective reading shows up only as the absence of a per-member rule; both of those are ours to fix, not yours.

mixed: the group-level burning is right - lantern group as agent, mire-essence consumed, past tense, the compound decomposed - but no per-member rule was emitted, so a lantern named later cannot be shown to have burned anything. Your wording (a definite plural with a distributive verb) already licenses that rule, so this is a translator-side omission and no rewrite would help.

good. "Together" correctly keeps one produce event over the lantern group with no per-member distribution, and mist-light is decomposed to its genus. Note only that "Together" itself gets no atom - the collective reading is carried by the absence of a distribution rule, which is indistinguishable from having forgotten one.

mixed: the showing, its theme and "at night" are all covered, but as with the burning the definite plural subject got no per-member rule, so no individual lantern's showing is derivable. The wording is fine; this is a translator-side omission, not something a rewrite fixes.

bad: "The mist-light" is a specific definite, yet it fills the agent slot with the bare kind symbol for mist-light rather than a referent, so nothing ties this mention to the mist-light the lanterns produced two sentences earlier. Rewrite as "The lanterns' mist-light attracted nightmoths." - the possessive mints a typed individual and links it back to the lanterns that made it.

mixed: the crowd is built correctly (a crowd whose members are nightmoths) and "gathered" rightly stays collective on the group, but "A crowd of nightmoths" is indefinite, so it mints a second nightmoth group with no connection to the moths the mist-light just attracted. If they are the same moths, write "A crowd of the nightmoths gathered at the Harbor Row." - the partitive "of the" makes the crowd a subset of the attracted group.
good. the three sky-cats become a counted group, both compounds get their genus atoms, the source is recorded, and the descent distributes to each cat through a fireable rule.

mixed: agent group, crowd, summer and tense are all covered with a fireable per-member rule, but "at the Harbor Row" was attached to the hunting event while the same phrase in the next sentence was read as modifying the crowd - your sentence leaves that attachment open. If you mean the hunt took place there, front it: "At the Harbor Row, the three sky-cats hunted the nightmoth crowd in summer."
good. the crowd is the right coreferent, "shrank" is read as an internal change of state with the crowd as the thing that changes, and "at the Harbor Row" is kept as the crowd's own location.

mixed: the survival itself is faithful, but nothing links the survivors to the crowd that was hunted - they are a fresh, unconnected nightmoth group - and no per-member rule was emitted. If the survivors come from that crowd, write "Some of the nightmoth crowd survived the hunt." - the partitive makes them a subset of it.

mixed: the flight is faithful (survivors as agent, the Hollows as goal, past tense) and "the surviving nightmoths" correctly reuses the group that survived, but the plural subject again got no per-member rule, so one moth's flight is not derivable. The wording is fine; no rewrite needed.

bad: "reached the Hollows" is a bare direct object, but it was slotted as a spatial goal - the role reserved for a "to"-phrase - so a "what did they reach?" query will not match it, and the per-member rule is missing here as well. The adjacent "fled to the Hollows" most likely pulled the role across, but the sentence itself is ordinary English and no rewrite improves it - this one is ours to fix.
good. the molting has the cats as the ones that change, the hunt as the containing interval, and a fireable per-member rule so each cat's molt is derivable.

bad: the threads are slotted in the role for objects that are created, destroyed or changed, although leaving them on a lantern displaces them unchanged, and the plural subject again got no per-member rule. Neither is caused by your wording - the sentence is clear as it stands - so no rewrite is warranted; both are translator-side fixes.
